basic_identification.sector_category: Water Resources / Hydropower Structures (approved by the Water Resources Division Council and finalized by the River Training and Diversion Works Sectional Committee, WRD 22, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: River Training and Diversion Works Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies standard guidelines, parameters, data requirements, and layout criteria for planning and designing river powerhouses integrated with barrages (barrage powerhouses) to optimize water utilization, determine power-generation layouts, and establish geotechnical and hydrological design boundaries.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Subsurface investigation for foundations — Code of practice (second revision)

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Criteria for investigation, planning and layout for barrages and weirs
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Establishes unified criteria for layout planning of diversion headworks that must integrate seamlessly with the barrage powerhouse structure.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Geological exploration for gravity dams and overflow structures — Code of practice
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Regulates systematic rock mass exploration, mapping, and core recovery protocols.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)

allied_standards.title: Criteria for Structural Design of Spillway Training Walls and Divide Walls
allied_standards.relevance: A sister hydraulic structure standard regulating guide walls, training walls, and divide walls which are integrated with the barrage and powerhouse to direct flows.

allied_standards.title: Recommendations for Design of Trash Racks for Intakes
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates the structural design and vibration limits of trash racks installed at the powerhouse intake bays to keep debris from entering turbines.

allied_standards.title: Guidelines for De-icing System for Hydraulic Installations
allied_standards.relevance: Specifies compressed air bubbler systems integrated near gates and trash racks to prevent ice build-up in freezing weather.

allied_standards.title: Safety in Construction, Operation and Maintenance of River Valley Projects — Guidelines — Part 11: Underground Excavation (First Revision)
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates safety, drainage tunnels, and rock stress-monitoring during tunneling or underground powerhouse excavations.

allied_standards.relevance: Provides design and planning requirements for flood protection levees, which secure the bounded powerhouse area from river flooding.

allied_standards.title: Hydrometric Determinations — Flow Measurement in Open Channels Using Structures — Flat-V Weirs
allied_standards.relevance: Specifies guidelines for Flat-V weirs used to measure flow discharge, helping evaluate river flow availability.

allied_standards.title: Guidelines for Fixing Intensity of Irrigation
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates irrigation water budgeting and intensity determinations, which directly dictate the 10-daily diversion requirements at the barrage.

allied_standards.title: Guidelines for Estimation of Flood Damages
allied_standards.relevance: Defines scientific procedures to survey, compile, and evaluate direct and indirect flood losses, supporting cost-benefit analyses of the protective barrage works.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel code in India, regulating support framing, steel gantry assemblies, and connection detailing for draft tube gates, intake gates, and powerhouse structural assemblies.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Design and Planning Guidelines (Water Resources Department / Diversion Works)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 14592 (Part 1) : 1998 is an engineering guideline for civil and electro-mechanical planning rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its site-investigation steps, soil boring counts, and water scheduling is strictly mandated in public sector tenders for run-of-the-river or low-head hydro projects (under CWC, NHPC, SJVN, state power corporations, and irrigation departments) to obtain technical clearance and validate Detailed Project Reports (DPRs). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Requires compiling and evaluating information regarding the high flood level (HFL) using physical flood marks and local field enquiries to define safety elevations against powerhouse flooding.
Mandates collecting detailed data on 10-daily irrigation withdrawals at the proposed barrage, if any, to coordinate power generation schedules with agriculture diversion demands.

Requires establishing a gauge (stage) and discharge relation curve extending up to the design flood level, based on historical field data covering at least five (5) years, but preferably supported by observations and acceptable extrapolation.

Requires compiling daily rainfall data from all rainfall gauging stations situated within and around the local catchment area, covering as many years of historical record as possible to support design flood estimations.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value (such as river stages, discharge rates, rainfall counts, or geological coordinates) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained must be identical to the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14592 (Part 1) : 1998 is the national Indian Standard guidelines specifying criteria for the site investigation, planning, and layout design of barrage powerhouses (low-head hydro stations integrated directly with river barrages). Formulated under the WRD 22 Sectional Committee, this standard unifies the engineering requirements for collecting vital baseline data during project pre-feasibility. It specifies that layout planning must compile and analyze historical high flood levels (HFL) from field marks, track 10-daily irrigation withdrawal requirements at the barrage, establish a 5-year minimum gauge-discharge relation curve up to the design flood, and aggregate long-term daily rainfall records across the entire catchment area, ensuring safe and hydraulically optimal powerhouse layouts.
